chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about a woman whom the enemy captured and raped until she died. He was asked: Is she in the rank of the martyr? He said: 'Yes, unless she assisted in bringing it upon herself.'

key_terms.أَعَانَتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا: Assisted in bringing it upon herself (voluntary consent)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who dies from rape during captivity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of *al-muhsana* (a woman captured and raped) as a martyr, emphasizing that her martyrdom is not negated by the physical act itself but by voluntary consent. The condition 'unless she assisted herself' is interpreted by Shia jurists to mean she did not willingly submit to the act, distinguishing her from one who was forced. This ruling underscores the principle of *khuruj al-irada* (loss of volition) in determining spiritual rank during captivity.
